questions.title: Anthropic SDK version pin strategy
questions.context: Codebase precedent for security-sensitive transitive deps is EXACT pin: svix@1.93.0, ts-morph@28.0.0, @tiptap/*@2.27.2. Loose caret is used for UI/utility deps (@clerk/nextjs ^7.3.4, @base-ui/react ^1.4.1, lucide-react ^1.16.0). audit-cache/ + audit-before-security-changes memory rule fires on every dep bump. SDK is the AI trust boundary — every Claude call routes through it.

options.label: Exact pin (e.g. "@anthropic-ai/sdk": "0.65.1")
options.description: Matches svix/ts-morph/@tiptap precedent. Reproducible builds; security-patch upgrades require deliberate bump + audit. Recommended.

options.label: Caret range (^0.65.1)
options.description: Auto patch-bumps on pnpm install. Faster security fixes but risks unannounced behavior shifts in a 0.x SDK that still moves quickly.

options.label: Tilde range (~0.65.1)
options.description: Allows patch only, not minor. Middle ground but doesn't match any existing dep style — adds a fourth strategy to the codebase.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: lib/ai/client.ts singleton shape
questions.context: SPEC R1 says: 'lib/ai/client.ts exports a getAnthropicClient() singleton (server-only, reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from env)'. Codebase precedent: lib/db/index.ts exposes a module-top eager const `db`; lib/auth/context.ts uses a per-request `await auth()`. Pure function/singleton matters for vitest mocking ergonomics (Q-22).

options.label: Lazy module-level singleton — `let cached: Anthropic | null = null; export function getAnthropicClient() { return cached ??= new Anthropic({ apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY! }) }`
options.description: Defers env-var read until first call (testable without setting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in unit tests). Mock by stubbing the function via vi.mock('@/lib/ai/client'). Matches the SPEC's getAnthropicClient() naming.

options.label: Eager module-top const — `export const anthropic = new Anthropic({ apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY! })`
options.description: Fails fast on missing env (Next.js build-time crash if env missing). Mirrors lib/db/index.ts pattern. Less flexible for testing (env must be set even in mocked tests).

options.label: Per-request instantiation — `export function getAnthropicClient() { return new Anthropic(...) }`
options.description: Trivially mock-friendly. Wasteful: Anthropic SDK is ~stateless but holds a connection pool. Performance penalty on a serverless route is real.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: lib/ai/cache.ts prompt-cache helper shape
questions.context: SPEC Constraint: 'Prompt caching mandatory on Q&A (system prompt + policy library block, cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" })'. CLAUDE.md ALWAYS rule #4: 'Use prompt caching on all repeated Claude API system prompts'. So Draft + Consistency Check also cache. cache.ts is the abstraction over Anthropic's `system: [{ type: 'text', text, cache_control: { ... } }]` array shape.

options.label: Minimal const + builder — exports `EPHEMERAL_CACHE = { type: 'ephemeral' } as const` plus `buildCachedSystem(text: string)` returning the full `[{ type, text, cache_control }]` array
options.description: Each endpoint imports `buildCachedSystem(SYSTEM_PROMPT)` and passes to `messages.create({ system: ... })`. Centralizes the shape; trivial to extend if Anthropic adds TTL options.

options.label: Two-block composer — `buildQACachedSystem(staticPrompt, policyLibraryBlock)` returns the full two-block array with cache_control on the policy library block only
options.description: Q&A is the high-volume cache target (60-80% hit-rate goal). Two-block split lets the static prompt cache separately from the per-org policy library. Tighter to the actual Q&A surface; less reusable for Draft/Consistency.

options.label: Skip cache.ts entirely — inline the cache_control object literal at each call site
options.description: Less abstraction. Easier to grep for `cache_control` in the codebase. Repeats the literal in 3+ places. Loses the central place to add TTL handling later.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Where model IDs live as constants
questions.context: Model IDs are locked by ADR-005/006/015: claude-sonnet-4-6 + claude-haiku-4-5-20251001. They appear in 4 endpoint files (draft, summary, qa, consistency). If/when a model is deprecated and we ADR-XYZ a swap, one update site is much cheaper than four.

options.label: Dedicated `lib/ai/models.ts` — exports `MODEL_SONNET = 'claude-sonnet-4-6'`, `MODEL_HAIKU = 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'`
options.description: Single grep target for model migrations. Mirrors POLICY_CATEGORIES const in new/actions.ts. Recommended.

options.label: Co-located with prompts in `lib/ai/prompts.ts`
options.description: Prompts and models change together for a given surface; co-locating makes the SURFACE the unit. Mixes concerns slightly (prompts are content; models are model selection).

options.label: Inline at each endpoint
options.description: Self-contained route handlers. Higher maintenance cost on model migrations. Doesn't match the constants pattern elsewhere.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Anthropic SDK mock approach for vitest
questions.context: Phase 3 mocking pattern (app/(admin)/policies/[id]/actions.test.ts:25-33): vi.mock('@/lib/policies/transitions', () => ({ submitForReview: ... })) with hoisted vi.fn() instances. SPEC requires unit tests for prompt-constant verbatim match, citation parser, tier-check math, 503 error contract, publishPolicy graceful-degrade. Cache-hit fixture also required (Q-25).

options.label: Mock the lib/ai/client wrapper — `vi.mock('@/lib/ai/client', () => ({ getAnthropicClient: () => mockAnthropicClient }))`
options.description: Tightest match to the Phase 3 vi.mock('@/lib/policies/transitions') pattern. Mock surface is just one function returning an object with `messages.create()` + `messages.batches.{create,retrieve}()`. Trivial to extend per-test.

options.label: Mock the SDK directly — `vi.mock('@anthropic-ai/sdk', () => ({ default: vi.fn().mockImplementation(...) }))`
options.description: Tests the wrapper too (Anthropic constructor + auth handling). More setup boilerplate. Useful only if the wrapper has logic worth testing — which it shouldn't if Q-02 is option (a).

options.label: MSW (Mock Service Worker) at the HTTP layer — `mockAPI.intercept('https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages', { ... })`
options.description: Most realistic mock (intercepts the actual HTTP). Adds msw as a dev dependency (new package — ASK FIRST gate). Heavier setup; overkill for SMB-scale tests.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Consistency Check batch-state tracking: separate table or column on ai_generations?
questions.context: SPEC explicitly defers this to discuss-phase: 'stores the returned batch.id against a new row in a batch_jobs table OR stores it in an ai_generations row with type="consistency" and result="PENDING:<batchId>" placeholder until completion (choice deferred to discuss-phase as a HOW question; SPEC locks the OBSERVABLE contract).' ADR-018-spirit doesn't bind ai_generations (no @ts-expect-error guard), but SPEC says 'one ai_generations row with type="consistency" written ON COMPLETION, not at submission'.

options.label: New `batch_jobs` table — `(id, orgId, anthropicBatchId, type='consistency', status, createdAt, resultJson)`
options.description: Clean separation: ai_generations stays SUCCESS-ONLY (preserves the 'one row per successful Claude call' semantic from CLAUDE.md ALWAYS rule #5). Pending state lives in batch_jobs. Adds a new migration (0004_batch_jobs.sql) + new repository module. Future batch surfaces (e.g., bulk Q&A reanalysis) reuse the same table.

options.label: Add `batchId` column to ai_generations — row inserted at submission with `result='PENDING:<batchId>'`, UPDATEd on completion with real JSON result
options.description: Fewer tables. But: violates 'one row per SUCCESSFUL Claude call' (a pending row isn't a successful call). UPDATE on a row counted by tier-limit math complicates the calendar-month counts. Adds 1 column migration.

options.label: Hybrid — store batch metadata in a small `batch_jobs` table (option a) AND mirror final result into `ai_generations` on completion (the canonical 'one row per successful Claude call' is still written at completion time)
options.description: Both tables stay clean. batch_jobs is the pending state machine; ai_generations is the success ledger. Two writes on completion (one transaction). Highest semantic clarity; marginal extra code.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Q&A content extraction from TipTap JSON
questions.context: Phase 3 03-CONTEXT.md D-05 deferred content-keyword search to Phase 4: 'Phase 4 will likely add an extracted_text column (extracted from contentJson on publish) + tsvector index.' Q&A endpoint must send policy CONTENT (not just title) to Claude. Token costs scale with content size. TipTap JSON has marks/attrs noise that wastes tokens.

options.label: Use @tiptap/html `generateHTML(contentJson, [StarterKit, Link])` then strip tags to plain text at Q&A query time
options.description: Reuses Phase 3's TipTap+StarterKit dep. Per-Q&A-call cost (~5ms for 100-policy library). No migration. Hot path. Recommended IF token-economy is the only concern.

options.label: Add `extracted_text` column to policies — populated by publishPolicy auto-hook (same fire-and-forget pattern as TL;DR), Q&A reads pre-extracted text
options.description: Cleaner Q&A endpoint (no extraction in hot path). Migration 0004 adds column + backfill. Phase 3 03-CONTEXT.md DEFERRED hint matches this. Sets up Phase 4+ tsvector index for content keyword search. Adds extract-on-publish hook coupling to publishPolicy.

options.label: Walk the ProseMirror JSON tree directly in `lib/ai/qa-extract.ts` — recurse over `content[]` collecting `.text` nodes
options.description: No HTML intermediate (fewer bytes, no marks/attrs noise). ~30 lines of code. Lock TipTap node-type coverage (text, hardBreak, etc.). Hot path stays in JS, no extra dependency.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: AiGenerations repository method set
questions.context: SPEC Boundaries: 'ai_generations repository body (Phase 2 ships skeleton): insert, countByTypeInMonth, findByBatchId (for Consistency polling).' Current skeleton has listAll + record (throw-stub). countByTypeInMonth is the tier-check math support; findByBatchId is consistency polling.

options.label: Minimal SPEC set: `insert`, `countByTypeInMonth`, `findByBatchId` (3 methods, plus existing listAll)
options.description: Matches SPEC exactly. countByTypeInMonth filter: `org_id=$1 AND type='draft' AND created_at >= start of current calendar month UTC`. Tightest contract; downstream callers can request more if needed.

options.label: SPEC set + `listByType(s, type, limit?)` for future admin debug UI
options.description: Adds an admin-only debug listing (e.g., 'most recent 50 Q&A calls'). Useful for ops but no Phase 4 success criterion needs it. Defers tightening of method surface.

options.label: SPEC set + `updateResultForBatch(s, batchId, resultJson)` if Q-06 picks option b (column on ai_generations)
options.description: Required if Q-06 lands on the in-row PENDING/UPDATE flow. Otherwise unused. Should be deferred to AFTER Q-06 is locked.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Policies.updateSummary method signature
questions.context: SPEC Requirement 3: 'updates policies.tldrSummary via the Policies repository'. Existing repository pattern (policies.ts:107-118): `updateDraft(s, id: PolicyId, patch: { title?, category?, contentJson? })`. The summary-update is a single-field write triggered by AI summary endpoint after Anthropic returns.

options.label: Dedicated method — `updateSummary(s, id: PolicyId, summary: string)`
options.description: Single-purpose. Matches `Policies.incrementVersion` and `Policies.statusCounts` precedent. Easy to grep ('who writes to policies.tldrSummary?' returns one site).

options.label: Extend updateDraft with optional `tldrSummary?: string` field
options.description: Fewer methods. But ADR-005 / SPEC says tldrSummary is AI-generated only, never user-supplied via draft edit. Mixing concerns; tests/types.ts D-07 invariant forbids tldrSummary in Policies.create — same spirit applies here.

options.label: New method on a separate `PoliciesAi` repository in `lib/db/repositories/policies-ai.ts`
options.description: Strict separation: AI-generated columns live in their own repository. Higher cohesion but adds a file + slight indirection. No existing precedent.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Citation block delimiter format in Claude's Q&A response
questions.context: SPEC Constraint: 'the Q&A system prompt is amended to instruct Claude to format citations as a trailing structured block (e.g. --- CITATIONS ---\n[{title, id}, ...]\n--- END CITATIONS ---) the parser can extract'. The exact delimiter is HOW — Claude's parsing reliability vs cleanliness of output trades off.

options.label:
Plain-text fence: `

--- CITATIONS ---
[{title, id}, ...]
--- END CITATIONS ---`
options.description: Per SPEC example. Easy to parse with simple regex. Claude can wrap the JSON in this fence reliably (well-tested pattern). Slightly noisy in raw output if delimiters leak.

options.label: XML tags: `<citations>[{title, id}, ...]</citations>`
options.description: Anthropic's official prompting best-practice recommends XML for structured outputs. Cleaner; easier for Claude to emit correctly. Parse with regex on tag boundaries. Slight risk if model emits stray `<` characters elsewhere.

options.label: Structured outputs via Anthropic's tool use feature — Claude calls a synthetic `cite_policy(id, title)` tool
options.description: Strongest schema enforcement. Requires `tool_choice: { type: 'tool', name: 'cite_policy' }` and structured response handling. Adds latency (tool-use round-trip semantics) and tokens. May not yet be stable on Claude 4.6 prompt-cached paths.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Citation parser failure mode (missing or malformed delimiters)
questions.context: Even with prompt engineering, Claude can occasionally drop the citation block (esp. for the 'I couldn't find information' branch where citations=[] is correct). Parser must distinguish 'no citations because no match' from 'parse failure because Claude broke format'.

options.label: Tolerant — return `{ answer: <raw text>, citations: [] }` when delimiters absent; log warning server-side
options.description: Maximum availability. Matches the 'no-match' answer-text invariant (which has citations=[] too). Distinguishes via the answer-text exact-substring match. Console.warn for ops visibility.

options.label: Strict — throw `CitationParseError` if delimiters present-but-malformed; tolerate when delimiters fully absent
options.description: Two failure modes: 'no citations' (delimiters absent → citations=[]) vs 'broken format' (delimiters present but JSON unparseable → throw). The throw bubbles to 503. Loud signal but rejects user's actual question on flaky model output.

options.label: Always-attempt-parse with regex fallback — first try fenced JSON, then regex for `[id]` mentions in answer text
options.description: Highest extraction recall. Risk of false-positive citations from natural mentions. Recommended only if Q-10 picks option (a) plain-text fence.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Published-policies query caching strategy for Q&A
questions.context: Q&A endpoint fetches all org's published policies on every call to build the prompt library block. ADR-006 prompt-cache covers Anthropic-side cost (60-80% cache-read on the policy block). DB-side cost is the second consideration. SMB scale: 25-300 employees × ~50-200 policies typical.

options.label: Direct DB query per call — `Policies.listPublishedForOrg(s)` returns rows; no app-layer cache
options.description: Simplest. Each Q&A round-trips a SELECT (~5-15ms on indexed orgId+status). ADR-006 prompt-cache absorbs the Anthropic-side cost regardless. No invalidation logic. Recommended for SMB scale.

options.label: Next.js `unstable_cache` keyed on `(orgId, maxUpdatedAt)` — invalidated when any policy's updatedAt changes
options.description: Saves DB round-trips on hot-tab Q&A bursts. unstable_cache name suggests API instability. Adds invalidation complexity (must call `revalidateTag` from every publishPolicy and editPublished). Marginal benefit at SMB scale.

options.label: In-memory per-server-instance LRU cache (e.g., Map) with 60s TTL
options.description: Vercel serverless: per-isolate cache, lifetime ≤ ~15 minutes per isolate. Pollution risk across orgs unless keyed carefully. Marginal at SMB scale; complicates cross-org isolation testing.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Policy library block format inside the prompt (sent to Claude)
questions.context: PROMPTS.md shows `--- COMPANY POLICIES ---\n{orgPolicyLibrary}\n--- END POLICIES ---`. The format inside {orgPolicyLibrary} is gray. Anthropic's prompting docs recommend XML for structured content over markdown for retrieval. Token efficiency matters (cache-read input token cost).

options.label: XML — `<policy id="uuid" title="...">\n<content>...</content>\n</policy>` per policy, joined
options.description: Anthropic-recommended for retrieval/citation prompts. Helps Claude isolate each policy. Slightly more tokens than plain. Citation extraction maps cleanly from the id attribute. Recommended.
Token-cheapest. Reasonably parseable by Claude. Matches the outer PROMPTS.md fence style. Slight risk if a policy's content contains `===` (low).
Most token-efficient if content is already markdown-friendly. But our content is TipTap-extracted text or HTML-stripped — markdown semantics don't carry through. Familiar format for Claude.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: lib/stripe/products.ts single file vs split with limits.ts
questions.context: SPEC R6 says: 'lib/stripe/products.ts exports TIER_LIMITS exactly matching the constant in reference/TIER-LIMITS.md AND checkTierLimit(orgId, feature)'. BUT ADR-024 says: 'Tier gating is 403-at-API-routes ... via requireTier(feature, org) in lib/stripe/limits.ts (Phase 6).' Two different file paths in two locked decisions — discuss-phase resolves which lands in Phase 4.

options.label: Single file: `lib/stripe/products.ts` exports TIER_LIMITS + PlanTier type + checkTierLimit (per SPEC R6). Phase 6 adds requireTier helper to the SAME file
options.description: Honors SPEC's literal path. Compatible with ADR-024 if we read 'lib/stripe/limits.ts' as a Phase 6 mention that can be redirected to products.ts via a Phase 6 amendment. Minimal file surface.

options.label: Split: `lib/stripe/products.ts` (constants + types only) + `lib/stripe/limits.ts` (checkTierLimit + future requireTier)
options.description: Honors ADR-024's literal limits.ts path. Cleaner separation: constants vs predicate functions. Phase 4 ships both files; Phase 6 grows limits.ts with requireTier + the boolean-feature gates. Two-file overhead Phase 4 doesn't strictly need.

options.label: Three files: `lib/stripe/products.ts` (constants), `lib/stripe/limits.ts` (checkTierLimit math), `lib/stripe/gates.ts` (requireTier + 403/redirect helpers)
options.description: Maximum cohesion. Each file is single-purpose. Gates layer is wholly Phase 6 — Phase 4 ships only products.ts + limits.ts. May be over-decomposed for a small surface.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Tier-check enforcement: helper wrapper vs inline guard
questions.context: SPEC R6: 'All API endpoints call checkTierLimit BEFORE the Anthropic call; on allowed: false, return 429 (for usage-bound limits like draft) or 403 (for tier-bound features like Consistency Check).' That's a 4-call duplication. ADR-026 established typed-error pattern in lib/auth/errors.ts.

options.label: Inline guard in each endpoint — `const check = await checkTierLimit(...); if (!check.allowed) return NextResponse.json({...}, { status: 429 })`
options.description: No abstraction. Each endpoint owns its 429 vs 403 status + body shape. Easy to grep for tier checks. ~6-8 lines duplicated 4x.

options.label: Throw-based — `requireTierLimit(orgId, feature)` throws TierLimitExceededError; endpoint catches and maps to 429/403
options.description: Extends ADR-026 typed-error hierarchy with TierLimitExceededError (carries `feature`, `limit`, `current`, `requiredTier` for mapping). Mirrors the existing IllegalTransitionError pattern. Single catch in a shared error-mapping helper.

options.label: Higher-order wrapper — `withTierCheck(feature)(handler)` decorates each route's POST function
options.description: Most DRY. New abstraction (no existing precedent in the codebase). Adds indirection that's harder to grep. Useful if more cross-cutting concerns (logging, tier-check, error mapping) compose later.

options.label: Custom

questions.chat_more: Resolved 2026-05-21: paired with Q-16=a. Endpoint pattern becomes try { await requireTierLimit(orgId, feature); await anthropic.messages.create(...) } catch (err) { if (err instanceof TierLimitExceededError) return 429/403 with documented body; else (Anthropic failure) return 503 ai_service_unavailable. Extends ADR-026 typed-error pattern to lib/stripe/.

questions.title: Tier-limit error class location
questions.context: If Q-15 lands on (b) throw-based, the error class needs a home. lib/auth/errors.ts holds BootstrapError hierarchy. Tier limits aren't auth — they're billing/subscription gates. ADR-026 scoped error-discipline to lib/auth/ only ('other layers may adopt the same pattern with their own ADRs when their surface complexity warrants').

options.label: New `lib/stripe/errors.ts` exports `TierLimitExceededError`
options.description: Domain-cohesive: stripe layer owns tier errors. ADR-026 'extend pattern when warranted' fits — Phase 4 IS the warranting moment. Add scripts/check-error-discipline.ts to scan lib/stripe/ too (drop the lib/auth/-only restriction).

options.label: Add to existing `lib/auth/errors.ts`
options.description: Single error-class home. But: auth scope creep (tier checks are not auth checks). ADR-026 explicitly scoped lib/auth/ — co-locating new domains breaks the boundary the ADR drew.

options.label: New top-level `lib/errors.ts` for cross-domain shared errors
options.description: Most flexible. No precedent yet. Better for v2 when 5+ domains have typed errors. Premature for Phase 4 (only stripe is joining the pattern).

options.label: Custom

questions.chat_more: Paired with Q-15=b. lib/stripe/errors.ts exports TierLimitExceededError (carries feature, limit, current, requiredTier for response mapping). scripts/check-error-discipline.ts gate extended to scan lib/stripe/ too.

questions.title: Anthropic error mapping: shared helper vs inline per endpoint
questions.context: SPEC R7: 'All 4 endpoints wrap the Anthropic call in try/catch and on ANY SDK error (network, 5xx, rate limit RateLimitError, content filter, timeout) return HTTP 503 with body { error: "ai_service_unavailable", retryAfter: 30 } AND header Retry-After: 30.' 4 endpoints × identical contract.

options.label: Inline try/catch + NextResponse.json in each endpoint
options.description: Each endpoint self-contained. Status + headers visible at the call site. ~10 lines duplicated 4x. Tests easy (each endpoint has its own 503 test).

options.label: Shared helper `lib/ai/errors.ts` exports `ai503Response()` returning the canonical NextResponse
options.description: Single source for the 503 envelope. Endpoint imports and returns the helper inside catch. Changes (e.g., retry-after value) update one site. Less duplication.

options.label: Higher-order wrapper `withAnthropicErrorMapping(fn)` that all endpoints' core logic runs inside
options.description: Wraps the inner Anthropic call (not the whole route). Centralizes the try/catch + 503 mapping. Hides the catch from each endpoint. New abstraction; subtle if a route needs to discriminate Anthropic-failure-with-context.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Anthropic failure logging format
questions.context: Phase 3 precedent: `console.error('[createPolicyAction] failed: ${detail}')` (lib/policies/transitions.ts implicit; actions.ts:135). Phase 7+ observability will replace console with structured logger. Phase 4 needs interim consistency.

options.label: Per-endpoint prefix — `console.error('[ai/draft] anthropic failed', { error })` etc.
options.description: Matches Phase 3 [createPolicyAction] prefix style. Grep-friendly. Object literal makes the error structured for Phase 7+ JSON-log migration.

options.label: Single prefix `[ai]` — `console.error('[ai] anthropic call failed', { endpoint, error })`
options.description: Lower noise in logs. Endpoint surfaced as a field. Slightly harder grep ('[ai/draft]' wouldn't match).

options.label: Minimal — just `console.error(err)` (let Phase 7+ logger reshape)
options.description: Least code. Loses the gate-context prefix Phase 3 standardized on. SF-M1 PR-review finding pattern argued the opposite (surface err.name + message + gate context).

options.label: Custom

questions.title: publishPolicy auto-trigger of TL;DR: synchronous vs fire-and-forget
questions.context: SPEC R3: 'publishPolicy in lib/policies/transitions.ts invokes the summary generation logic (via an internal generateSummaryForPolicy(policyId, ...) helper, not a self-HTTP call) AFTER the state transition commits; summary failure is logged but does NOT roll back or fail publishPolicy — policies.tldrSummary stays null and admin can regenerate later.' AFTER commit + non-failing — sync vs fire-and-forget is HOW.

options.label: Synchronous after commit — `await generateSummaryForPolicy(...)` inside publishPolicy, wrapped in inner try/catch that logs and continues
options.description: Caller waits for both transition AND summary. Haiku is fast (~1-3s). Admin clicking Publish sees the TL;DR populated in the same request. Slight latency cost. Failure-logged-not-thrown matches SPEC literally.

options.label: Fire-and-forget — `void generateSummaryForPolicy(...).catch(err => console.error(...))` after commit
options.description: Caller returns immediately after state transition. Summary populates async (admin refreshes to see). Less latency on Publish action. Risk: Next.js serverless may terminate the isolate before the promise resolves (Vercel Pro+ has waitUntil; Hobby may cancel).

options.label: Sync with explicit timeout — `await Promise.race([generateSummary(...), timeout(10000)])` with timeout catch
options.description: Bounds latency. Adds complexity (timeout cancellation semantics). If timeout fires, summary stays null — same end state as failure. Marginal benefit over (a) given Haiku's typical 1-3s response.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Consistency Check admin page URL
questions.context: SPEC R5: 'Admin Consistency Check page at /admin/consistency (or /dashboard/consistency, exact path is HOW for discuss-phase)'. Phase 3 D-01 locked the admin URL convention: NO `/admin/*` prefix — admin routes are concrete URLs like `/dashboard`, `/policies`. middleware ADMIN_URL_PATTERNS gates them.

options.label: `/dashboard/consistency` — nested under /dashboard
options.description: Matches Phase 3 D-01 convention (no /admin prefix). Sidebar nav can group it under Dashboard. middleware ADMIN_URL_PATTERNS already covers /dashboard(/|$) — zero matcher changes. Recommended.

options.label: `/consistency` — top-level admin URL
options.description: Shorter URL. New ADMIN_URL_PATTERNS regex entry needed. Sidebar item is a peer of Policies. Sets precedent for future admin tools (`/reports`, `/users`).

options.label: `/policies/consistency` — under /policies
options.description: Groups with the policy library it analyzes. Natural mental model. middleware /policies(/|$) matcher already covers it. Slight URL semantic clash (it's not a policy).

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Consistency Check polling UX
questions.context: Anthropic Batch API typical latency is 5-30 minutes per their docs. Admin must wait. SPEC says client polls — no Phase 4 cron infra. UX choices: auto-refresh frequency vs manual.

options.label: Auto-poll every 30s via Client Component `useEffect` setInterval; visible 'Checking status...' indicator
options.description: Hands-off UX. Page open = admin sees result when ready. 30s × 30min = ~60 polls = 60 GET requests (cheap). Tab inactive: browser throttles to ~1min. Recommended.

options.label: Manual 'Refresh status' button only — admin clicks to check
options.description: Lowest network load. Admin context-switches and forgets. Worse UX. No background activity.

options.label: Auto-poll with exponential backoff — start 10s, double up to 2min cap
options.description: Balances responsiveness early (just-started batches sometimes complete fast) with thrift late. More complex client state.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Draft 'Generate with AI' form fields shape
questions.context: SPEC R2: 'PolicyEditor at /policies/new shows a Generate with AI button (admin-only); clicking opens a prompt-input dialog; on submit calls /api/ai/draft and pre-fills the editor with draftContent.' API takes `{ prompt: string, policyType?: string }`. Dialog form shape is HOW.

options.label: Two fields — `prompt` (textarea) + `policyType` (select dropdown from POLICY_CATEGORIES constant)
options.description: Matches SPEC API exactly. policyType reuses the same 8-category list from new/actions.ts. Minimal cognitive load. Recommended.

options.label: Three fields — `prompt` + `policyType` + `additionalContext` (the PROMPTS.md draft template has `{additionalContext}`)
options.description: PROMPTS.md template has `{additionalContext}` slot. Server can map: prompt='Write a {policyType} policy for a {companySize} {industry} company. {additionalContext}'. Adds inputs beyond SPEC's `{ prompt, policyType }` API shape — SPEC change needed.

options.label: Single prompt field — admin writes free-form 'Generate a remote work policy for our company'; backend infers policyType
options.description: Lowest friction for the admin. Loses the policyType structured field for SPEC's `{ prompt, policyType }` API. Goes against SPEC R2.

questions.title: Consistency findings UI rendering inside severity grouping
questions.context: SPEC R5: 'renders the polled result as a list of findings grouped by severity.' Severity grouping is LOCKED. Inside each group, the per-finding card has policy_a + policy_b + issue_type + description. Display density choice.

options.label: Collapsed by default — each finding card shows policy_a vs policy_b + issue_type + a 1-line description; click expands the full description
options.description: Compact list view for scanning. Admin can drill into one finding at a time. shadcn Collapsible or Accordion primitive. Recommended for libraries with 10+ findings.

options.label: Always expanded — full description inline; severity column / icon at left
options.description: Information-dense. Better for small finding sets (<10). Scrolling burden grows with finding count.

options.label: Table view — Severity / Policy A / Policy B / Issue type / Description (truncated)
options.description: Matches Phase 3 policies-list Table pattern. Sortable in theory (not in Phase 4 polish). Description truncation hides the most important field.

questions.title: verify:phase-4 composition relative to verify:phase-3
questions.context: Current verify:phase-3 is a 10-gate chain ending with vitest + .tmp cleanup. Phase 4 adds new gates: check:ai-layer (integration test against mocked Anthropic + TEST DB), check:ai-prompts (substring match vs reference/PROMPTS.md), possibly check:tier-limits.

options.label: verify:phase-4 wraps verify:phase-3: `pnpm verify:phase-3 && pnpm check:ai-layer && pnpm check:ai-prompts`
options.description: Phase-3 gates run first; phase-4-specific gates layer on top. Phase 3 stays untouched. Easy to roll back a phase-4 change without disturbing phase-3. Recommended.

options.label: verify:phase-4 replicates the full chain inline — copy verify:phase-3's commands + add new ones
options.description: Single command holds the complete contract. No nested invocation. Changes to verify:phase-3 wouldn't propagate to verify:phase-4 — explicit sync required.

options.label: Extend verify:phase-3 itself with the new gates (no separate verify:phase-4)
options.description: Single chain grows. Conflicts with ADR-029 (phase boundaries — main must be green for both verify:phase-3 AND verify:phase-4 as separate gates between phase squashes). Loses the per-phase boundary.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Cache-hit assertion fixture
questions.context: SPEC Acceptance Criterion: 'the Anthropic SDK response usage metadata on the 2nd successive POST /api/ai/qa against the same org's policy library reports usage.cache_read_input_tokens > 0 (provable via instrumented logs or unit-test fixture).' Mocking Anthropic loses real cache-hit telemetry — must fake it.

options.label: Vitest fixture — mockAnthropicClient.messages.create called twice: 1st returns `{ usage: { cache_creation_input_tokens: 1000, cache_read_input_tokens: 0 } }`; 2nd returns `{ usage: { cache_read_input_tokens: 1000, cache_creation_input_tokens: 0 } }`. Test asserts the 2nd call's response carries cache_read > 0
options.description: Pure unit test. Verifies the endpoint reads/exposes the cache_read field. Does NOT verify Anthropic actually caches — that's an integration concern. Recommended for Phase 4 unit tests.

options.label: Integration test against the live Anthropic API in `pnpm check:ai-layer` (no mock)
options.description: Real cache-hit verification. Costs money (Sonnet 4.6 ~$3/1M tokens). Slow (5-15s per call). Flaky on CI. SPEC suggests this option but lists it as 'instrumented logs or fixture' — fixture is the chosen path.

options.label: Skip the assertion — log inspection only (Phase 7+ observability stack will pin the contract)
options.description: Defers to a future phase. Loses falsifiable check at Phase 4 ship. Risk: regression on cache_control opt-in goes unnoticed.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Prompt-substring verification gate implementation
questions.context: SPEC Acceptance: 'lib/ai/prompts.ts exports 4 prompt constants; each contains the exact verbatim text from reference/PROMPTS.md (verifiable via a substring match on a 40-char anchor per prompt).' New gate, separate from vitest.

options.label: `scripts/check-ai-prompts.ts` (ts-morph) — extracts the 4 string-literal exports from lib/ai/prompts.ts; reads reference/PROMPTS.md; asserts each constant's text contains a hardcoded 40-char anchor from PROMPTS.md
options.description: Matches ADR-026 ts-morph precedent (check-error-discipline.ts, check-policy-id-brand.ts). One-shot CI gate. Recommended.

options.label: Vitest test in `lib/ai/prompts.test.ts` — imports the constants, reads PROMPTS.md via fs, asserts substring match
options.description: Same logic but inside vitest. Slightly slower (vitest startup). Easier to debug locally. Loses the dedicated gate signal.

options.label: Inline assertion at module-load time in `lib/ai/prompts.ts` — `if (!PROMPTS_MD.includes(anchor)) throw new Error('drift')`
options.description: Crashes the route handler if drift. Loads PROMPTS.md from disk at runtime (file-system access in serverless). Not viable for production.

questions.title: API-SPEC.md amendment for citation shape — ADR or no ADR?
questions.context: SPEC's Notable cross-contract impact: 'Decision in Round 2 to use structured citations ({ title, id }[]) deviates from reference/API-SPEC.md line 45 (citations: string[]). Phase 4 ship MUST include an amendment to reference/API-SPEC.md documenting the new shape.' The question is whether this rises to a new ADR or stays as a SPEC.md+API-SPEC.md doc-only change.

options.label: Doc-only — amend reference/API-SPEC.md inline, reference Phase 4 ship in the amendment commit
options.description: No new ADR. SPEC.md captures the decision rationale (R2 'Failure Analyst' row). API-SPEC.md is reissued frozen-contract with the new shape. Lighter weight; matches SPEC's 'cross-contract impact' framing.

options.label: New ADR-030 — 'Q&A citation shape from string[] to { title, id }[]'
options.description: Adds the change to .planning/intel/decisions.md and PROJECT.md <decisions> block. Forward-discoverable via the ADR catalog. More ceremony for a single SPEC-derived contract shift. Adds to the locked-decision count.

options.label: Both — doc amendment + ADR-030
options.description: Maximal transparency. Redundant if the ADR rationale lives in SPEC.md anyway. Higher friction; matches the Phase 3 ADR-026/027/028 pattern of treating non-trivial contract changes as ratified decisions.
